channel.title: Natural Sciences Museum Science Café Events
channel.description: Science Café events from the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Science Trivia (Jun 4, 2026)
item.description: What’s cooler than absolute zero? The answer is Science Trivia night at NCMNS! Questions feature a mix of science facts, current news, pop culture and scientific discoveries. Held in the Daily Planet Cafe the first Thursday of each month, this is a great opportunity to mingle with friends, compete for prizes and bragging rights, and perhaps even learn something cool. The Museum closes at 5 PM; the Daily Planet Cafe will remain open. Please copy the URL below to share this page!

item.title: STEM Comedy Night (Apr 24, 2026)
item.description: It’s not every day that these stand-up comedians with questionable STEM backgrounds get to fully geek out about their favorite things. With backgrounds ranging from archaeology to engineering these funny folks are finally in their element at the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences. They’re not giving a dissertation. item.title: Science Café: Illuminating AI Night (Apr 16, 2026)
item.description: Curious about what data science and AI bring to your life everyday? Join us for an evening discussing exciting local research from scientists at the NC Museum of Natural Sciences, UNC-Chapel Hill, UNC’s Renaissance Computing Institute (RENCI), NC State University, and beyond! item.title: Teen Science Café: Monster Rockets (Apr 10, 2026)
item.description: This presentation compares the three biggest rockets ever built—the legendary Saturn V that took humans to the Moon, NASA’s powerful Space Launch System (SLS), and SpaceX’s ambitious Starship. Learn how these giants stack up in size, power, design and mission goals. Also, discover how each represents a different era of space exploration and our evolving plans to explore the Moon, Mars and beyond. Alan Rich is a retired scientist and engineer now working with NASA as a JPL Solar System Ambassador...

item.title: Teen Science Café (Apr 10, 2026)
item.description: Teen Science Cafés bring teens together in an informal setting to learn about science and technology. Cafés happen from 6pm to 7pm the first Friday of each month during the school year. Each café will include a scientist presentation, an interactive activity relating to the discussion, a Q&A session, and time to socialize with other teens who enjoy science.
